status.notes: Retired: the GT code is only the two-line answer binding — a bare weighted coin flip over {1, 2} — and the Gaussian mixture model the original prompt described is never implemented or referenced (hollow witness). The original prompt also handed the solver the exact answer binding and its probabilities verbatim. No salvageable task: there is no model code to make load-bearing via respec, and the remaining content is trivial and fully leaked. Worklist verdict 'kill' confirmed.

Retired 2026-07-07: vacuous — the bare utterance 'fish' maps to the sole fish object (blue fish) with probability 1.0, so the literal listener alone determines the answer and the RSA adds nothing. Trivially solvable, no pragmatic content. (atom-2, the context-uncertainty variant, is kept.)

Retired: structurally identical to forestdb-kids-scope/atom-1 (same RSA pipeline, same parameters, same probabilities [0.506, 0.494]) — only the utterance label 'two-not' vs 'every-not' differs. This adds no independent test signal; the worklist verdict is 'kill'. Statement fields are empty per the retired-record convention.

Retired: standard MCMC cannot converge on this degenerate-manifold posterior. The posterior concentrates on the 1D curve point2 = 10*w/(1-w) within a 200-wide prior; independent chains from different initial positions explore different manifold regions, producing W1 floor 0.80 >> cap 0.16 regardless of sample count (tried 5000 to 1000000 samples, HMC, larger burn-in). All chains get stuck near their starting values due to the tight Gaussian likelihood (sigma=0.1). ex2.2/ex2.3 were already retired; ex2.4 (rejection sampling) passes cleanly; ex2.5 has the same issue and is also retired.

The 2D joint distribution over (point2, inter) pairs is ill-posed as a finite-domain distribution (TV=1 across seeds because every float-valued support point is unique). Respeccing to a well-posed query would drop point2 (whose marginal is ill-posed; W1 floor=55) and keep only interpolationWeight, which is identical to the ex2.1 respec — making this a duplicate. Retiring to avoid redundancy.

The GT output is a 100-element MCMC chain trace (trajectory) of pointInMiddle values with lag=0, intended to demonstrate autocorrelation. Trajectories have no valid algebra representation. Any marginal respec using these inference parameters is ill-posed (W1 floor=6.06), because 100 samples with lag=0 and poor mixing produces wildly inconsistent empirical distributions across seeds. No salvageable well-posed query exists for this code.

Retired: same degenerate-manifold MCMC issue as ex2.1. uniformDrift with width=0.1 on point2 in [-100,100] is too slow to mix; W1 floor for interpolationWeight marginal is 0.45 >> cap 0.12, and for point2 the floor is 161 >> any reasonable cap. Tried increasing samples to 200000+, changing drift width, HMC -- all fail because the posterior is a 1D manifold and chains are initialized randomly across the full prior space. Dropping point2 from the record does not rescue the problem since interpolationWeight and pointInMiddle marginals are also ill-posed under these settings.

The GT output is a distribution over pairs of 4-element real vectors (two Dirichlet simplex topic vectors) from MCMC. Per SCHEMA.md, dist over realvec is not supported in v1, and treating the continuous float tuples as finite labels gives TV≈1 across seeds (no two MCMC samples share identical float coordinates). Worklist flagged migration_difficulty: redesign. Retire rather than author a hollow or unscorable record.

Retired as a mathematical duplicate of ex2.1: both model the same causal support posterior over the same observed data, and after respec both reduce to identical marginals (P(relation), mean cp, mean b). The only difference is the MCMC efficiency trick (marginalizing E analytically via an inner Infer rather than forward-sampling it), which is purely an implementation detail with no effect on the mathematical answer. No distinct problem can be authored here.
